definition: Circumscribe means to restrict someone's powers, choices, or scope within narrow limits.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circumscribe. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circumscribe should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The scholarship's fine print circumscribed her choices: three approved majors, one campus, and no semesters abroad.
Curb is milder than circumscribe: a curb checks one impulse or expense, while circumscribing draws a boundary around the whole field of action.
Imprison goes further than circumscribe: a circumscribed life is hemmed in but still moving; a prisoner's walls end the question.

Restrict is the everyday, all-purpose word for holding something within limits — restrict parking, restrict sugar, restrict access. Circumscribe is its formal cousin and adds the image of a drawn boundary enclosing a whole scope: powers, rights, a life. You restrict one thing; a charter circumscribes what a ruler may do at all.

Confine keeps a person or thing physically inside a space — a cell, a pen, a sickroom. Circumscribe draws its line around abstractions instead: powers, choices, ambitions held within narrow bounds. A quarantined patient is confined; a regent whose every decision needs the council's approval is circumscribed.

Circumscribe literally means to draw a line around: whatever sits inside the circle may move, but never past it.
Where limit is flat and factual, circumscribe emphasizes the closed boundary — powers, options, or a whole life held within narrow bounds.
Circumscribe suits writing about powers, rights, and lives held within drawn bounds — charters, constitutions, biographies.
For physical or casual squeezes, use constrain (this unit); for the vivid image of chains dragging at someone, use fetter (this unit).
